evidence: Walked every criterion in all five judge.toml files (2 gate, 42 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual = 54). Overall the rubric is strongly outcome based and browser decidable. (1) No criterion asks for a source read: every prompt line 1 says 'Use rendered UI and ordinary browser-observed product data only. Never inspect app source, bundles, filesystem, database files or implementation code.' (2) Durable evidence: state-changing legs are read back from an independent browser context or after reload/restart, e.g. gates/constraints/judge.toml hro_gate_shared (Observer in a new context finds the job and exactly one card), functional hro_add_candidate/hro_arrive_bottom/hro_reorder/hro_bulk_move/hro_undo_restores ('Mei Lin's independent context reads the same order'), hro_notes (Observer reads both notes), hro_msg_exchange (Tomas's independent context), hro_restart (restart_app then fresh sign-in, seeded order Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi / Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz and Noor's note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' - verified against seed APP-105/106/108, APP-103/104 and notes[0]). (3) Refusals are decided by server-observable replays with fresh version values and same-kind positive controls (functional prompt.md lines 17 and 23: 'what is graded is that the server refuses it and nothing changes'), and refused actions are tied to a durable trace (no card/order/message change, no Activity line; hro_activity_refusals). No response-shape-only assertion exists: hro_anonymous pairs the 401 (stated in hireops_rules.md section 1) with 'nothing changes'; hro_candidate_private is a privacy outcome the rules define on received payloads (rules section 7 'Nothing a candidate's browser receives may contain...') with own-data and staff-read controls. (4) Probes are distinctive: every board protocol uses the judge's own suffixed jobs/cards; stale-move probe C is an ABA replay (F Applied->Screen captured, Mei moves F back to Applied, replay) that only a real per-card version (rules section 3 'Every card carries a version') can refuse; polish note example 'Call back on Fri' and the 'distinctive' replies are absent from seed and golden (grep count 0 in seed_data.json and all solution app/public and src files); Lena's starting unread of 1 matches seed (3 messages in APP-301, read_count 2 for USR-CAN3). (5) Time-varying legs define the observation: 'within 15 seconds ... accept the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds' (functional V/U), document.activeElement and getBoundingClientRect().top reads (hro_refused_put_back, hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_earlier_place). (6) Visual 'looks right'-style judgement is confined to likert craft rows with five described anchors naming concrete surfaces (board, conversations, activity, candidate view), which the skill's check 41 accepts; no binary row says 'looks right'. INSTANCE FOUND (P3, real but bounded): functional hro_thread_access decides the hiring-manager read restriction by UI absence: 'a manager of another job (Ingrid) cannot open it (not listed, or refused)', and protocol T line 39 says only 'as Ingrid ... check it is not available or refused'; the prescribed replays for Ingrid cover sending only ('Replays of Rafael's send request ... in the sessions of the Observer, Ingrid and Noor Haddad'). Rules section 6 says a hiring manager reads 'only in conversations of their own jobs; the others are refused'. 'Not listed' is a probe that leaves no server-side trace, unlike the parallel candidate leg in hro_candidate_private, which replays the staff read. Minor latent observation (P3, not counted as a defect): hro_pol_failed_send offers context.setOffline as the fallback for non-HTTP sends; Chromium offline emulation is not reliably applied to an already-open WebSocket, so a socket-send conforming app might not experience a failure. The golden sends through fetch (public/js/app.js:29) and shows 'The message was not sent; it is still here.' (threads.js:194), so the reference path is decidable. Runtime: no configured GLM judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'); the scripted golden run (workspace.json, all groups passed) shows the outcomes are observable in a browser for the golden but is not a judge decidability measurement.
counterexample: A plausible broken app filters the conversation list by hiring manager but its conversation-read endpoint has no job-manager check: Ingrid sees no J2 conversation in her list, so hro_thread_access passes ('not listed'), yet a direct read of Tomas's J2 conversation in Ingrid's session returns all messages, violating hireops_rules.md section 6 'the others are refused'. Send replays are refused, so nothing in the row detects the leak.
suggested_fix: In hro_thread_access and protocol T, require replaying Rafael's observed read of Tomas's J2 conversation in Ingrid's session (refused or not found, no messages returned), with Rafael's identical read as the control, instead of accepting 'not listed' alone.
